cand.title: Arajet is scheduled to start three weekly direct Montevideo–Punta Cana flights on 3 March 2027.

quote.assumption: exa agent fixed effort=high (contact enrichment not included)

findings.namedBuyers: Priority relationship candidates: Jessica Weinerth, Arajet Vice President of Sales and Distribution, for channel/partnership routing; and Alejandra de la Cuadra, Hiperviajes head of product, quoted on Uruguay-origin Punta Cana demand and the new direct service. Neither is verified as the holder of a hotel contract or room block. Alejandro Grieco, Arajet Country Sales Manager Argentina, is an additional route-informed referral candidate, not a verified Uruguay account owner.
findings.futureEdition: Within the requested horizon: scheduled route commencement is 3 March 2027, supported by Arajet, Carrasco Airport and Uruguay’s Tourism Ministry. Important direction distinction: Arajet advertises Punta Cana→Montevideo from 3 March and Montevideo→Punta Cana from 4 March; 4 November 2026 trade reporting also gives 4 March for the latter. The general announcements give three weekly frequencies, Mondays/Thursdays/Saturdays, but do not resolve the direction-specific timetable. The airline’s launch promotion was sold 11–18 August 2026 for travel 3 March–31 October 2027; the sales promotion is expired, not the future route. That travel window is neither an event duration nor proof the route ends in October. No event edition or operating commitment through May 2028 was verified.
findings.hotelProductFit: Inference using the supplied hotel brief: the 620-room Uvero Alto all-inclusive is a plausible guestroom-led leisure, family, friends-group or small incentive option for Uruguay arrivals, rather than a large conference venue. Hiperviajes reports that its Uruguay-origin Punta Cana customers mostly choose all-inclusive and approximately seven nights; this is market context, not a forecast or room block for Wyndham Alltra. Modest meeting space argues against pursuing a large plenary-led congress. Airline staff/crew accommodation should be treated separately and is not evidenced here.
findings.venueCommitments: The historical announcement took place at Carrasco International Airport in Montevideo. It is not a Punta Cana meeting venue or accommodation commitment. No launch reception venue, host hotel, incumbent crew hotel or route-specific hotel block was identified in the reviewed sources. No evidence establishes that Wyndham Alltra or a competing hotel holds this candidate’s lodging demand.
findings.historicalRotation: Not applicable as an edition-rotation series: this is a new airline route. The 2026 Carrasco announcement is a past promotional activity, not an upcoming hotel event. No recurring conference, destination rotation or historical host-hotel timeline was verified.
findings.accommodationSourcing: Hotel sourcing is unconfirmed, not open. Arajet publicly accepts group-airfare enquiries for 10+ passengers at groups@arajet.com and charter enquiries at charters@arajet.com; these are air-sales channels, not hotel RFPs. Its ancillary-services page states that hotels and other services are offered by external partners, with final terms controlled by those providers. Hiperviajes is an evidenced Uruguay distribution prospect, not a confirmed buyer of this hotel or a contracted operator of this route. No named local DMC, lodging procurement agent or open allotment request was verified.
findings.organizationStructure: Arajet, S.A. is a Dominican commercial airline and the route operator, not an association, PCO or DMC. Carrasco/Aeropuertos Uruguay is the airport partner and Uruguay’s Tourism Ministry is a public-sector stakeholder. Hiperviajes is a travel agency; its product team is commercially distinct from the airline. No event planner or hotel-accommodation buyer has been appointed in the reviewed route announcements.
findings.competitiveLimitations: Demand cannot be allocated to Wyndham merely because passengers fly into Punta Cana: the route also serves onward connections, and travel agencies describe Cap Cana, Bayahibe and La Romana as alternative resort destinations. PAM Hotels announced an Arajet alliance with cross-discounts, but its own published 15% offer expired 31 October 2026. This is historical competitive-channel evidence, not proof of a live 2027 exclusive, Montevideo allocation, incumbent event hotel or displaced Wyndham demand. No sourced sell-out, overflow or room-shortage evidence was found.
findings.recommendedSalesAction: Approach Jessica Weinerth to identify the Uruguay commercial lead, group/series distributors and hotel-partnership owner; use groups@arajet.com only for the air component. In parallel approach Alejandra de la Cuadra at Hiperviajes to test a seven-night all-inclusive Uvero Alto proposition. Offer a date-specific net-rate/group proposal only after confirming distribution, payment/cancellation terms, airport transfers, expected passengers and who contracts lodging. Ask whether a launch familiarization trip is planned; do not represent one as announced. Verify the 3 March outbound/4 March Uruguay-origin distinction before pricing, and ask whether any PAM benefits or exclusivity extend into 2027. Retain as airline/trade development unless a real lodging brief is obtained.
findings.currentEditionAccessibility: As of 14 November 2026 there is no verified current-edition hotel opportunity. The August announcement has passed; flight sales and a scheduled future route do not demonstrate an accessible accommodation tender. Airline group-airfare and travel-trade relationship channels are accessible, but hotel sourcing and buyer authority remain unconfirmed.
findings.futureCompetitiveCapturePotential: Inference: pursue Uruguay-origin leisure/group distribution for arrivals from 4 March 2027, plus later departures only after the relevant flight operation is confirmed. This is ongoing account development, not annual event capture. A partner-packaging precedent exists, but the PAM offer’s October 2026 expiry and absence of verified exclusivity leave its 2027 competitive effect unresolved. Do not forecast room nights from frequencies, aircraft seats or another market’s load factor.
